quizName: DMV Practice Test #14 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What does making eye contact with other drivers mean?

options.text: They will definitely yield to you.
They do not necessarily see you.
It is not worth the effort.

questions.correctAnswerText: They do not necessarily see you.
questions.explanation: Do not assume a driver will yield just because you make eye contact. A driver may look directly at you and still not notice you.

questions.question: What should you do if your rear tire locks up?

options.text: Try to speed up while braking.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the rear brake.
questions.explanation: To regain control when your rear wheel locks, release the brake. However, if the rear wheel locks on a surface with good grip, you can keep it locked until you stop completely.

questions.question: Why should you practice using convex mirrors?

options.text: Most people are not used to mirrors.
They make objects look farther away than they actually are.
They make objects look closer than they actually are.
It is hard to remember to look at them while riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: They make objects look farther away than they actually are.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors give you a wider view of the road behind you. They make objects appear farther away than they really are. Get used to how your mirrors work if your motorcycle has convex mirrors.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Follow me
questions.explanation: Hand signals help riders in groups communicate with each other. This signal means "follow me."

questions.question: What should a motorcycle rider do because motorcycles are hard to see at night?

options.text: Stay directly in front of other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: To ride safely at night, slow down, increase your following distance, use the headlights of cars ahead to see the road, use your high beam (unless following or meeting another vehicle), and adjust your lane position as needed.

questions.question: When turning with a three-wheeled motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Stay in the center of the lane.
Stay on the outside of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change your path as needed.
questions.explanation: A three-wheeled motorcycle or motorcycle with a sidecar turns differently than a two-wheeled motorcycle. The best path may require you to move from the outside of the curve to the inside before straightening out.

questions.question: When turning on a motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Press the grip in the direction you want to turn.
Press the grip opposite of the direction you want to turn.
Do not hold the grip because it is dangerous.
Do not lean the motorcycle because it is unsafe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the grip in the direction you want to turn.
questions.explanation: When riding faster than walking speed, your motorcycle must lean to turn. Pressing the grip in the direction you want to turn will make the motorcycle lean the right way.

questions.question: How should you apply the front brake?

options.text: Squeeze the lever firmly and gradually increase pressure.

questions.correctAnswerText: Squeeze the lever firmly and gradually increase pressure.
questions.explanation: Use all four fingers to squeeze the front brake lever firmly and smoothly, applying more pressure gradually.

questions.question: What does an integrated braking system do?

options.text: Applies partial rear braking when you use the front brake.
Applies partial front braking when you use the rear brake.
Applies equal braking to both brakes when either is used.
Remembers how hard the rider usually brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Applies partial front braking when you use the rear brake.
questions.explanation: An integrated braking system automatically applies some front braking when you use the rear brake. Check your owner's manual for details about your motorcycle's braking system.

questions.question: What kind of sign is rectangular in shape?
questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign
questions.explanation: Signs that show traffic rules, like speed limits, are usually rectangular with white background and black text or symbols. You must follow the rules shown on these signs.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Slow or stop
questions.explanation: A rider can use hand signals instead of or with turn signals. When a rider's left arm is bent at the elbow and pointing downward, it means the rider plans to slow down or stop.

questions.question: If you must swerve, you should:

options.text: Press the handgrip in the direction of the turn.
Press the handgrip in the opposite direction of the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handgrip in the direction of the turn.
questions.explanation: To swerve and avoid danger, press gently on the handlegrip in the direction you want to turn. To swerve left, press the left grip, then the right to straighten. To swerve right, press the right grip, then the left.

questions.question: If the road is wet, you should avoid:

options.text: The left portion of a lane.
The center portion of the lane.
The right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: Oil from cars collects in the center of lanes. When the road is dry, this provides enough grip for motorcycles. When wet, avoid this center strip. You can ride to the side and still stay in your lane.

questions.question: Small vehicles can appear ______ and seem to be traveling ______ than they actually are.
questions.correctAnswerText: Farther away, more slowly
questions.explanation: Small vehicles like motorcycles can look farther away and moving slower than they really are. This makes it hard for other drivers to judge their true distance and speed.

questions.question: When looking through a turn to see where you are going, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Turn just your head.
questions.explanation: When turning, look toward where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: When riding in a group, what does it mean when the lead rider raises their left arm and extends their index finger?

options.text: The group will pull off at the next exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in a single-file formation.
questions.explanation: Hand signals help riders communicate in groups. When the lead rider raises their left arm and points with one finger, it tells the group to form a single line.

questions.question: When you are being passed from behind, you should:

options.text: Ride in the center portion of the lane.
Ride in the left portion of the lane.
Ride in the right portion of the lane.
Ride in any portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: When being passed, stay in the center of your lane. This discourages the other driver from moving back into your lane too soon.

questions.question: When braking, you should:

options.text: First apply the front brake, then the rear.
First apply the rear brake, then the front.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes together every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black text or symbols. They alert drivers to hazards and road conditions ahead.

questions.question: If riding a three-wheel motorcycle in a group, you should travel in a:
questions.correctAnswerText: Single-file line.
questions.explanation: Two-wheel motorcycles usually use a staggered formation in groups. Three-wheel motorcycles are too wide for this. They should travel in a single-file line instead.

questions.question: More than half of all crashes involve:

options.text: Riders with less than six months of experience on their motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riders with less than six months of experience on their motorcycle.
questions.explanation: More than half of all motorcycle crashes involve riders who have had their motorcycle for less than six months.

questions.question: In hot weather, wearing a riding jacket:

options.text: Helps protect against heat exhaustion and dehydration.
Should be avoided because it causes heat-related problems.
Should only be worn if it is a light color.

questions.correctAnswerText: Helps protect against heat exhaustion and dehydration.
questions.explanation: Wear a riding jacket and long pants in hot weather. They provide safety protection and help prevent heat exhaustion and dehydration.

questions.question: When planning a long group ride, which idea should NOT be used?

options.text: Plan travel distances based on the least experienced rider.
Skip breaks so riders reach their destination faster.
Place inexperienced riders behind the leaders.

questions.correctAnswerText: Skip breaks so riders reach their destination faster.
questions.explanation: Plan route length based on your least experienced rider. Take regular breaks to reduce fatigue. Place inexperienced riders behind the leader so experienced riders can watch them. Ride in a staggered formation.

questions.question: To reduce your reaction time, you should:

options.text: Ride slower than the speed limit.
Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.
questions.explanation: Ride carefully when approaching an intersection. Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes to react quickly if needed.

questions.question: The best protection for a rider is:

options.text: Keeping distance between your motorcycle and other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keeping distance between your motorcycle and other vehicles.
questions.explanation: The best way to avoid crashes is to stay far away from other vehicles. Keep plenty of space so you have time to react to other drivers' mistakes. Wearing proper gear is also important for safety.
